speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Just in case Members thought it was over.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is the first full Budget delivered after GE2020.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is the first Budget session for the first-term constituency Members of Parliament and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament, as well as the newly appointed Nominated Members of Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But it is helpful to look beyond these facts and figures to the values which we have upheld in approving this Budget.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our endorsement of the COVID-19 measures reflect our determination to bring Singaporeans safely through this pandemic and to build resilience.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We agreed on the approach to open up safely, bring our economy back to normalcy and provide targeted support for affected sectors, businesses and workers that remain hard-hit by the pandemic.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We rightly acknowledged the invaluable contribution of our healthcare workers in the fight against COVID-19 and the tremendous debt of gratitude we owe them for the sacrifices they have made and continue to make.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We wholeheartedly supported the salary enhancements for healthcare workers, with Members putting forward suggestions for enhancing the career prospects and progression opportunities for nurses and healthcare professionals.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We recognised that even as we tackle the immediate challenges presented by COVID-19, we have a rare window of opportunity to act to position ourselves to emerge stronger for a post-pandemic world.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We focused on helping our businesses and our workers to ride the winds of change, to look forward, not back, but providing the necessary support to see them through.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members noted the need for companies to adjust to major structural shifts, such as accelerated digitalisation, rising protectionism, remote working and the reconfiguration of supply chains, as well as the need to seize new opportunities in growth areas and plug into critical parts of emerging business opportunities.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We affirmed support for business transformation, growth and innovation as well as cross-border collaboration.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We considered how to help SMEs leverage digital solutions and other resources and through collaboration with GLCs and MNCs to help them scale up and venture into global markets.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We were concerned for our workers and the need to prepare them for the jobs of tomorrow while paying close attention to those in sunset industries, to help them to reskill and gain access to opportunities in growth industries.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Labour Members of Parliaments laid out proposals to better protect jobs and empower and support vulnerable workers such as the low-wage workers and senior workers.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members remained concerned about job security and employability of Singaporeans, highlighting issues such as increased competition from foreign manpower, unfair hiring practices and workplace discrimination and put forward many suggestions to address these.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MOM in reply, spoke about the legal and regulatory measures that are in place to keep our workplaces progressive, fair and inclusive.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We reaffirmed our commitment to be a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: COVID-19 has increased inequalities and the impact of the digital divide.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members called for greater support to ensure social mobility and to bridge gaps, especially for the lower income.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The expansion of ComLink will be a critical step towards achieving these objectives.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We affirmed our support for children with special education needs and students from disadvantaged families.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will build capabilities and leverage technology to provide more seamless and integrated support for lower-income households.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We put the spotlight on mental health, which has been made worse worldwide by COVID-19.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We agreed to enhance mental health services, improve outreach and intervention, and provide a supportive environment for those with mental health issues.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today is International Women's Day, but MSF has gone further, declaring 2021 as the year of celebrating SG Women.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The women Members of Parliament rose to the occasion – quite literally – by standing to speak in sisterhood on women's issues.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this Budget, we also signalled clearly that the little red dot has a big green agenda.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Climate change adaptation and sustainability have taken the forefront in our plans for the future.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These have been consolidated into the Singapore Green Plan 2030, which was debated in the joint segment in the Committee of Supply as execution will be across different ministries.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We were agreed on future plans and the need to do more to support Singaporeans.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, all these good things need to be paid for.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, a crucial part of the debate was on our fiscal strategy.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, Government is called upon to do more.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: How do we fund all the good things we want to do going forward?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members welcome the use of borrowing to finance the cost of nationally significant infrastructure such as new MRT lines.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The long lifespan of such infrastructure makes it equitable to distribute the cost across different generations who will benefit directly from it.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa also suggested funding economic investments to help us emerge stronger through one off special purpose borrowing.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For recurrent expenditure, however, the Government reiterated that it should be funded through recurrent revenue.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Even before COVID-19, we had already signalled the need to raise GST to fund the anticipated structural increase in healthcare spending correlated to an ageing population.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Alternatives such as wealth taxes were proposed and discussed.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some Opposition Members of Parliament suggested tapping on land sales proceeds, or using 100% of the NIR instead of 50%, both of which essentially involve using more of our reserves.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I wish only to leave Members with this thought: if we want to do more for our people, we will have to spend more.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On behalf of the House, I would also like to thank you, Mr Speaker and your deputies for presiding with great stamina over the proceedings.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: You have taken pains, Mr Speaker, to be fair and even-handed to Members of Parliament on both sides of the House.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are also grateful to the Clerk of Parliament, the Parliament Secretariat and the staff for their support behind the scenes.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members should be aware that for every late night spent in the Chamber, the Parliamentary staff have to stay even later to ensure that all is in order for the next day's proceedings.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A big thank you also to the translators who have had to follow the speeches in two languages simultaneously.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And I would also like to express our thanks to the teams from Speedoc Pte Ltd, BGC Group Ptd Ltd and Chye Thiam Maintenance Ptd Ltd who – if you are wondering what they did – facilitated the smooth running of the Antigen Rapid Testing in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I was curious, I asked my Parliament colleagues as to which had the highest number of cuts.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I was told that there was one year there were 700-over cuts, but please do not get any ideas.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The important thing is not to mistake volume for quality.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Last year has been extraordinary and it continues to be challenging.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think it is just for all of us to share a big word of thanks to all public offices out there for serving our country diligently.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Before I share some reflections from this Chair to round up the debates, you would have noticed that some Ministers like to distribute this or distribute that before their speeches.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, because of FOMO (Fear of Missing Out), I also would like to do the same.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, Mr Speaker, may I have your permission to distribute some handouts to our fair Members on occasion of today being International Women's Day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is only for the women, so the men, please.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am sure the roses are suitably disinfected as well.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, if I may put this to all of you in Parliament, the question is that, "This being the year of celebrating our better halves in family and society, we, the lesser halves here in Chamber, present a small token to say thank you to all our ladies here, whether serving as Members of Parliament, Non-Constituency Members of Parliament and Nominated Members of Parliament, Clerks, interpreters and our wonderful assistants".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As many as of the opinion say aye.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We continue to strengthen our efforts over the years.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Today, we have high literacy rates, low maternity mortality rates, high life expectancy, high full-time employment rates or just simply providing a safe environment for our womenfolk to operate in.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I raise this as a first reflection – that what we do is often built on the hard work of all our predecessors.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In our yearly Budget and Committee of Supply debates, we rightfully dive into the weeds because details do matter.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There will always be areas that we can do better in as we seek to ever improve and to introduce new initiatives and new ideas.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Let us not also forget the efforts by many that have come before us.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Let us not just latch onto one negative issue or another negative issue and just forget completely all the wonderful work that has been done over the years.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Let us remember the giants on whose shoulders we stand.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In the 2018 COS wrap up speech, I talked about not missing the woods for the trees.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think this analogy is particularly apt this year, given the concerns over the developments in Clementi and Kranji.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Let us all have a sense of perspective and context.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there genuine concerns with what has happened?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think I share the horrors that many felt when we read the news and saw the clips on the forest being cleared when permit was not given.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But is our green conversation just about this alone?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do we not forget that we live in an island state that is just 40-plus km east to west, 20-plus km north to south.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For those of you who are familiar with the game SimCity, I think you will know exactly what is at stake.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As Senior Minister Teo shared, the trade-offs are real, and often, the choices are difficult.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: By all means, please do grapple with the Clementi and Kranji issues, but do ask ourselves which other country in the world even comes close to having to make these difficult choices, both as a city and as well as a nation?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And despite the constraints that we have, do actually take a look and read what has been done and what will be done under the green plan.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The deep division and polarisation that we saw in the recent, very bruising US Presidential campaign serve as a reminder to never take what we have for granted, and how very easily things can go south.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have also seen how politicians in many countries wave the anti-foreigner flag often enough, whether accurately or not, just to get people stirred up.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The sad truth is that these efforts actually work and the temptation to play these political games are very real.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do we want to play to the gallery and distil everything down to a provocative speech, an emotive meme, an inflammatory post?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Or do we want to listen, sense-make, address head-on, the issues that are in front of us?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Make the right and often difficult tough choices, and help to carry our people along.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In my maiden speech as Speaker, I said that Parliament needs to be a beacon from where Singaporeans can take reference with confidence when addressing and understanding issues that will matter greatly for our collective well-being.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, my third reflection is how we conduct our business in Parliament, what we say and how we discuss the issues matter a great deal.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We need to help our people understand why we do what we do.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We can agree, we can disagree, we can agree to disagree, but to do so in a way that edifies and not spiral to the lowest common denominator.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: My concluding reflection is that I am grateful for who we are and what we have.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There are no throwing of chairs and slippers and fists.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We may debate and argue but it has always been with a decorum befitting our Parliament, and I thank you for it.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There is also a growing consciousness and passion for not just the material development of our country but also our heart and soul.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The fact that we have moved on from slaying sacred cows to fiddling with Minister Lawrence Wong's sacred stones also reflects a sort of progress.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Remember how excited we all got when Minister Desmond Lee said that we will have parks within 10 metres of all our homes?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This was about as rousing as Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's very intimate sharing of his feeling very dangerously close to agreeing with Minister Chan after his Committee of Supply (COS) speech.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But unfortunately, it was 10 minutes and not 10 metres from the park and our Assoc Prof did not quite totally agree with everything But it is not bad.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Politics is such that people like to focus on the negative and the tensions because it makes for better news.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But there is much positivity and alignment that we can also celebrate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As a collective leadership body here in Parliament, we need to ensure that we really do emerge stronger together across the aisle as well.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can we evolve a different democracy where even as we are divided by our political colours, we remain a strongly unified Singapore red?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I recently met with our Singapore ambassador to a well-respected and often admired developed country, which shall remain unnamed.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They had a deep regard for our efforts to ensure continued supply chain connectivity, especially of essential items.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Above all, they were struck by the trust and confidence in the Government.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They envied that this whole-of-society collaboration has strengthened Singapore to fight cohesively against the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There is indeed much that we can be proud of.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There is still much to improve on and there is much to do.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This year, I am not sure why Westlife's songs featured quite so prominently in the COS.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Even today, there were a couple of songs that were quoted.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I could suggest some versions: "Everybody Knows" that when "We are One", "Nothing is Impossible" as we go "Against all Odds" and make our "Dreams Come True".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But I would rather end with the lyrics from two Singaporean popular songs in Singapore, quoted by our two new Nominated Members of Parliament, Dr Shahira and Dr Tan Yia Swam.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: From Ilham Pujangga: "Kasih sesama manusia, Seperti anda sayangkan diri anda, Pandang yang satu kepada yang ramai sayang, Pandang yang ramai kepada yang satu." Love humankind as much as you love yourself, as how each individual beholds the community and as how the community beholds each individual.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Though I may be but one person and may not achieve much, I will do my very best to give what little I can.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And on those notes, thank you very much.
